intro: The PPF Calculator projects the maturity amount of a Public Provident Fund account in India, with yearly deposits, interest compounded annually, and a 15-year tenure.
uses: It is used to plan long-term tax-free saving, to see how much a yearly deposit grows over 15 years, and to compare the interest earned with the total amount deposited.
formula: Each year the balance grows as Balance = (Balance + Yearly Deposit) × (1 + Rate ÷ 100), repeated for the tenure. The calculator caps the yearly deposit at ₹1,50,000 and the tenure at 15 years, matching the PPF rules. Interest earned = Maturity amount − Total deposited.
example: Inputs: Annual Deposit = ₹1,50,000, Interest Rate = 7.1%, Tenure = 15 years. Step 1: deposit ₹1,50,000 each year for 15 years, so total invested = ₹22,50,000. Step 2: applying the yearly formula 15 times, the balance grows to ₹40,68,209. Step 3: interest earned = 40,68,209 − 22,50,000 = ₹18,18,209. The calculator uses a 7.1% rate; PPF interest rates are revised by the government — check the current rate.
howTo: Step 1: Enter the amount you will deposit each year in the "Annual Deposit (₹)" field — the maximum is ₹1,50,000.
Step 2: Enter the interest rate in the "Interest Rate (%)" field — the calculator defaults to 7.1%.
Step 3: Enter the tenure in the "Tenure (years)" field — 15 years is the standard PPF term.
Step 4: Tap Calculate to see the maturity amount, the total invested, and the interest earned.
tips: PPF has EEE tax status: the deposit, the interest, and the maturity amount are all tax-free, which makes it one of the most tax-efficient savings options in India.
Depositing early in the financial year earns more interest, because PPF interest is calculated on the lowest balance between the 5th and the end of each month.
The maximum deposit is ₹1,50,000 per year — depositing more does not earn interest on the extra amount.
After 15 years the account can be extended in blocks of 5 years, with or without further deposits.
mistakes: Entering a deposit above ₹1,50,000 per year — the extra amount does not earn interest.
Using an old interest rate as if it were fixed — the PPF rate is reviewed by the government and changes over time, so check the current rate.
Expecting to withdraw freely before maturity — partial withdrawals are allowed only from the 7th year and under conditions.
Confusing the 15-year tenure with a lock-in that can be shortened — the account matures after 15 years.

faqs.q: What is the current PPF interest rate?
faqs.a: The calculator uses 7.1%, which was the rate when it was built. PPF interest rates are revised by the government — check the current rate before planning, and enter it in the "Interest Rate (%)" field.

faqs.q: How much will I get if I deposit ₹1,50,000 every year for 15 years?
faqs.a: At 7.1% interest, the maturity amount is about ₹40,68,209. You deposit ₹22,50,000 in total and earn about ₹18,18,209 in interest, all tax-free.
Yes. PPF has EEE status: deposits qualify for deduction under Section 80C, the interest earned is tax-free, and the maturity amount is tax-free.

faqs.q: What is the maximum I can deposit in PPF each year?
faqs.a: The maximum is ₹1,50,000 per financial year. You can deposit it in one go or in instalments, but the total for the year must not exceed ₹1,50,000.
